design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 of auto_loan_servicing (category finance), env_0041_online_used_car_retailer.

[Step 0 - draw] `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/tasks/auto_loan_servicing --task 0` printed {"task": 0, "key": "env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/auto_loan_servicing/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6, 6]}. Assignment: deferral fee (root) 6, returned-payment fee 6, deferral qualifying payment 5, late fee 4. `--tasks 2` also showed task 1 = 1 prerequisite problem, factor counts [6, 4].

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: finance_ext_returned_payment_fee, finance_ext_late_fee_assessment, finance_ext_deferral_qualifying_payment, finance_ext_deferral_fee and their tools assess_returned_payment_fee_ca20439d, assess_late_fee_56686208, pay_deferral_qualifying_amount_eaa14a46 (owner=user), grant_payment_deferral_f4f9e9cb. Reserved headroom for task 1 (1 prerequisite problem, a customer's own write): the goodwill relief of a paid late fee (finance_principal_credited) and the borrower's own cure payment of a past-due installment (scheduled-installment payment) - disjoint subjects/tools, a different ledger state (late fee already assessed and unpaid), so task 1 needs nothing claimed here.

[Why a good test] Teresa asks one thing: move her September installment to the end of the loan. The deferral fee rule says the fee is not fixed until a partial payment on the request date has cleared the fees and the accrued interest; the qualifying-payment rule says that payment is fixed only after every unpaid-after-grace installment carries a late fee and not until every returned payment carries its returned-payment fee. The ledger shows both are missing (the 2026-09-28 return has no fee; the 2026-09-23 installment passed its grace on 2026-10-03 with no late fee). So the agent must discover two state-due fees, compute each (4 and 6 factors), hand the customer her own payment with a 5-factor amount and split, then compute the 6-factor deferral fee on the world those writes produce. Difficulty is reading policy, reconciling a 28-entry ledger and stacking tiers - not tool guessing (each problem has exactly one tool, named by its policy).

[Design thesis] surface goal "move my September payment to the end of the loan" -> deferral fee (root) waits on qualifying partial payment -> qualifying payment waits on the late fee and the returned-payment fee -> observable terminal state: two fee entries, a partial payment entry + fee-paid entry, a deferral entry + deferral fee entry, contract fees 4.81, principal 19064.18, last payment 2026-10-05, next due 2026-10-23, maturity 2030-04-23, deferrals used 1. Depth 3 hops (D <- P <- {C, N}); breadth: registration state (purchase), vehicle program (purchase), KestrelCare service contract (warranty), maintenance plan (maintenance), 12- and 6-month windows of returns and late fees, earlier deferral entries, tenure counts, contract age, days past due.

[Problem-tree card]
- Root finance_ext_deferral_fee (agent, grant_payment_deferral_f4f9e9cb). Edge D -> P: kind value_input, gate partial_payments_today, form state, sentence "A deferral fee is not fixed until a partial payment posted on the request date has cleared the fees due and the interest accrued on the contract." (negated direction; the desk tells a borrower the deferral is not booked until...). Exactly one write of this difficulty posts a partial payment: pay_deferral_qualifying_amount_eaa14a46 (the cure tool posts scheduled-installment payments). Opening evidence: last_payment_date 2026-08-23, no partial-payment entry. Resolved by the customer (owner=user).
- P -> C: value_input, gate fees_outstanding, form state, "The deferral qualifying payment is fixed only after the loan history carries a late-fee entry naming every installment that is still unpaid after its grace period." (affirmative). Only assess_late_fee_56686208 books late-fee entries. Opening evidence: next_due_date 2026-09-23 unpaid (return of 2026-09-28), grace over 2026-10-03, no late-fee entry naming 2026-09-23.
- P -> N: value_input, gate fees_outstanding, form state, "The deferral qualifying payment is not fixed until the loan history carries a returned-payment fee entry naming every borrower payment the bank has returned." (negated). Only assess_returned_payment_fee_ca20439d books returned-payment fee entries. Opening evidence: return 8cd6...(2026-09-28) whose source payment has no fee entry naming it.
- Four-point test, each sentence: ordering connective (only after / not until), record-visible state on the waited side (an entry kind on the ledger, fees due, the last payment date), no tool/policy id/snake_case token, scope = 'every installment ... unpaid after grace' / 'every borrower payment the bank has returned' / 'a partial payment posted on the request date' exactly as the condition fields. Derivation: sentence + ledger (missing entries) + the depended-on rule (which says what entry it books) -> exactly one resolving write each.
- Topological order N, C, P, D; N and C commute (proved by a swapped-order run: same results and the same terminal hash). Deletion sensitivity: skip P -> deferral fee 7.81 (not 4.81); skip C -> qualifying payment 443.67 (not 512.55); skip N -> 457.55. user_scenario names none of these problems; tools validate none of them.

[Base-invariant card] Late fee and returned-payment fee writes (subject finance_fee_assessed): finance_payment_application.payment_active (status active - finance_contracts.status = active); finance_late_fees.after_grace (time: anchor finance_contracts.next_due_date 2026-09-23 = day 0, duration variants.payment_grace_days 10, calendar days, relation not_before, boundary exclusive; 2026-10-03 still in grace, 2026-10-04 first assessable day, 2026-10-05 passes); finance_late_fees.one_late_fee_per_installment (dedup on finance_contract_id + installment_due_date 2026-09-23: no late fee for that installment exists, and the returned-payment fee is not a late fee). Qualifying payment (finance_payment_posted): payment_active; card_limits (online bank transfer, not a debit card; no card payment this month). Deferral (finance_deferral_granted/applied): deferral_active; deferral_dpd (anchor next due date 2026-09-23 day 0, max 30 inclusive: 2026-10-23 last qualifying day, 2026-10-24 refused; 2026-10-05 = 12). Non-structured base conditions also hold: installments paid 17 >= tier B minimum 6; deferrals in 12 months 0 < 2; deferrals used 0 < 4; no due-date change in October.

[Business-object card] Contract 'fc' (the only finance contract). Returned-payment fee object = payment 68396be3 (2026-09-23) whose return 8cd6ea04 has no fee; the January return 3bbe9e94 is excluded because fee 33e1e2d4 (38.00) names its payment. Late-fee object = installment 2026-09-23; installments 2025-07-23 and 2026-03-23 already carry fees 12.50 and 13.19 (both paid); every other installment was paid within grace. Qualifying payment = all fees due at handling time (55.00 + 11.54) + interest from 2026-08-23. Deferral object = installment at the next due date 2026-09-23.

[Factor card] (tier taken / evidence / baseline figure of result)
- Returned fee (6): state schedule FL 30.00 (purchase registration_state; baseline 47.50); amount add-on 10.00 (return total 549.45 > 500; baseline 40.00); repeat-return x1.5 (returns 2026-01-27 and 2026-09-28; baseline 35.00); tenure credit 3.00 (17 paid; baseline 58.00); protection-plan credit 4.00 (warranty KestrelCare Gold financed + maintenance plan, multi-source; baseline 59.00); channel charge 2.00 (online_ach; baseline 53.00). Whole baseline 25.00 vs gold 55.00. Near-misses: the purchase order's selling_dealer_state is GA (Kestrel's Georgia hub) while the rule reads the registration state FL - a reader taking the dealer's state charges the Georgia and Texas fee and lands on 62.50; and the return entry's amount 351.93 (principal reinstated) against its total_received 549.45 - the rule's 'full amount' selects the large-return add-on (a reader using amount takes the medium add-on and 47.50).
- Late fee (4): FL percentage 4.0 (baseline 14.84); tenure reduction 0.5 (baseline 13.19); courtesy x0.6 (multi-source: 1 late fee in 12 months AND 1 return in 6 months; baseline 19.23); small-payment floor 10.00 (multi-source: payment 549.45 < 600 AND age 18 months; baseline 15.00). Whole baseline 27.47 vs 11.54. Near-misses: late fee 2025-08-03 is 14 whole months back (outside 12); return 2026-01-27 is 8 whole months back (outside 6); selling dealer state GA (a reader taking it gets the Georgia and Texas percentage and 16.48).
- Qualifying payment (5): standing 15 days (multi-source: 17 paid AND returns in 12 months; baseline 369.19); lateness x1.5 (2 late fees in 12 months once step 10 lands; baseline 455.21); program 2 days (purchase Kestrel Certified; baseline 493.44); delinquency 2 days (12 days past due; baseline 493.44); seasoning -1 day (18 months; baseline 522.11). Whole baseline 340.52 (interest + fees only) vs 512.55.
- Deferral fee (6): FL one-month interest method 5.54 (baseline 34.00); return-risk x1.5 (baseline 2.04); good-faith credit 3.00 (multi-source: 17 paid AND partial payment dated today; baseline 7.81); delinquency surcharge 2.50 (baseline 2.31); seasoning credit 1.00 (baseline 5.81); first-extension credit 2.00 (no earlier deferral entry; baseline 6.81). Whole baseline 25.00 vs 4.81. Near-miss: the purchase order's selling dealer state GA - the rule reads the registration state FL; a reader who takes the dealer's state applies the Georgia lesser-of method (25.00) and computes 34.00.
Cross-difficulty factors read seeded rows of purchase (purchase_orders FL / Kestrel Certified), warranty (service_contracts KestrelCare Gold financed in fc) and maintenance (maintenance_plans active, for the returned-fee protection-plan credit). Overrides are declared in each policy's overwrite (late fee formula, returned-payment fee, deferral fee); the qualifying payment has no base provision for its quantity (overwrite []).

[initial_state rows] customers (identity), purchase_orders (registration_state FL, selling_dealer_state GA as the near-miss, Kestrel Certified: 4 factors read it), finance_contracts (tier B, monthly 549.45, APR 12.09, principal 19236.21, fees 0.00, next due 2026-09-23, last payment 2026-08-23, contract 2025-03-10), finance_transactions (28 rows: funding; 19 scheduled payments; returns 2026-01-27 and 2026-09-28; late fees 2025-08-03 12.50 and 2026-04-03 13.19 and returned fee 2026-01-27 38.00, each cleared by the next payment's fee portion), service_contracts (KestrelCare Gold active financed), maintenance_plans (Standard, active). Removing the 2026-09-28 return removes both state-due fees and the tree; removing the service contract or maintenance plan moves the protection-plan credit; removing the purchase order breaks four state/program factors. Every historical fee equals what the extended policies give on its own date (seed_consistency rows). Automatic clauses checked: no further late fee is due (2026-10-23 not yet due), no payoff, no GAP, no unwind.

[Persona] Teresa is anxious and apologetic, volunteers only the goal and that the September payment 'never went through' (true: payment 2026-09-23 returned 2026-09-28). Identity (8135553417, 1987-06-14, 3862) on request; email/ZIP/car only if asked. Passive branches: pays herself, exactly as handed, only if told a payment is needed; accepts a deferral fee if told; ends when told the September payment is moved and the next due date. She never names a fee, a figure or a step.

[Standard solution] find_customers(8135553417) -> verify (phone, DOB, SSN4) -> find_finance_contracts -> find_finance_transactions -> find_purchase_orders -> find_service_contracts -> find_maintenance_plans -> unlock/call assess_returned_payment_fee (55.00, payment 68396be3, installment 2026-09-23) -> unlock/call assess_late_fee (11.54, installment 2026-09-23) -> unlock_user / customer calls pay_deferral_qualifying_amount (512.55 = 273.98 + 66.54 + 172.03) -> unlock/call grant_payment_deferral (2026-09-23, next 2026-10-23, maturity 2030-04-23, fee 4.81).

[Verification] The verification run (check_compute.py --task 0, which replays the gold writes with the real tools) replays the gold writes with the real tools and evaluates every compute on its handling-time world: returned fee 55.0 (baseline 25.0), late fee 11.54 (27.47), qualifying payment 512.55 (340.52), deferral fee 4.81 (25.0); per-factor baselines as in computations[].factor_sensitivity. Prerequisite sensitivity run: P without N 457.55, P without C 443.67, D without P 7.81; swapped N/C order -> identical results and terminal hash.

[Blind draft from visible context] Using only the rule prose, the tool docstrings, the persona and the finder returns: the deferral rule's prerequisite sentence sends the reader to the qualifying payment; its two sentences send the reader to the ledger, where the 2026-09-28 return lacks a fee and the 2026-09-23 installment is unpaid after grace; each fee rule then gives one number from the purchase order, the plans and the ledger windows; the payment and deferral figures follow. The draft reproduces 55.00, 11.54, 512.55 (273.98/66.54/172.03) and 4.81 with the same write order.

[Gates run for this task] From the repository root, with DIFF=env/env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/tasks/auto_loan_servicing: check_extended.py $DIFF --task 0 -> EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools.py $DIFF --task 0 -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks.py $DIFF --task 0 -> REPLAY OK (deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure = initial_state); check_solvability.py $DIFF --task 0 -> SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute.py $DIFF --task 0 -> COMPUTE OK (handling-time recompute = expected = gold, every factor baseline moves the result and equals factor_sensitivity, whole baseline = baseline_result); check_grounding.py $DIFF --task 0 -> GROUNDING OK; check_cache_diff.py $DIFF --task 0 -> CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap designed); check_cross_fire.py $DIFF --task 0 -> SCOPE OK. check_traceability.py is deferred until the KB is published.

[Revisions] r1: first draft had a historical deferral in 2025; dropped because tier rules (6 installments before a first deferral) and the qualifying-payment rule would have required a matching partial payment on that date - the deferral-count factor was replaced by the return-risk multiplier. r2: the qualifying payment's good-faith amount is applied to principal (the waterfall would send any amount beyond accrued interest and fees to principal), so the prose names it a good-faith amount rather than prepaid interest.
r3 (audit round 2, audits/policy_task/auto_loan_servicing): F-1 - the deferral maintenance-plan credit split on prepaid visits remaining, which no lender weighs for a deferral fee, was replaced by the first-extension credit (no earlier deferral entry 2.00, one earlier 1.00, two or more none), a standard servicing practice; the deferral fee becomes 4.81 (baseline 25.00) and the skipped-payment figure 7.81. Task-0 RED 1 (no near-miss in the deferral fee) - the financed purchase order now shows selling_dealer_state GA with transfer_distance_miles 455 (sold from Kestrel's Georgia hub, registered in Florida); the rules read the registration state, so a reader who takes the dealer's state gets 34.00 for the deferral fee, 16.48 for the late fee and 62.50 for the returned fee; no balance moves. O-1: the two qualifying-payment prerequisite sentences now say 'the loan history carries ... entry naming every ...' so an old, already-paid fee still satisfies them literally. O-2/O-3: the goodwill rule and tool no longer say 'a late fee the borrower has paid'. O-4: the goodwill counts are worded as exactly what they count (every waived late fee and every billing-correction credit). O-5: the returned-fee rule states that a fee not charged on the date of the return is charged on the date it is assessed. O-6: the cure payment's due-date advance is declared as an overwrite of the base sentence and keeps 'never beyond the maturity date'. Re-ran every gate (all OK). O-7 (multipliers labelled method) and O-8 (relationship credits, channel charge, program allowances) are kept as recorded observations: the instantiate contract names a multiplier on an intermediate as a method family, and the relationship and channel ladders are plausible servicing treatments the audit did not red-light; none moves a figure other than by its own documented tier.
user_scenario:
You are Teresa Navarro, 39, a dental assistant in Tampa, Florida. In September the clinic you work for cut your hours, and your September car payment on the 2021 Toyota RAV4 you bought from Kestrel never went through. You are calling Kestrel Auto Finance because you want to push your September payment to the end of your loan so you can get back on your feet; your October payment you can cover from your next paycheck. You speak warmly but a little anxiously, you apologise more than you need to, and you keep things practical.

You open by saying you are behind on your September car payment and asking whether that September payment can be moved to the end of your loan. You do not know your loan or account number. When the representative asks who you are, you give your mobile number 8135553417; when asked to confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1987-06-14, and the last four of your Social Security number, 3862. Only if they ask for something more, your email is teresa.navarro.tampa@gmail.com and your home ZIP code is 33611. If they ask which car, it is the 2021 Toyota RAV4.

You are happy for the representative to set up the change to your loan for you. If the representative tells you that you need to make a payment yourself before the September payment can be moved, you ask how much it is and you agree to pay it today from your checking account; when they hand the payment to you in the Kestrel app, you submit it exactly as they give it to you, with the same total, the same split between interest, fees and principal, and the loan reference they read out, and you read back the confirmation it shows. If they tell you there is a fee for moving the payment, you accept it without arguing. You do not know any of the amounts yourself and never suggest one. Once the representative confirms that your September payment has been moved to the end of your loan and tells you when your next payment is due, you thank them and end the call.
